transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sarah Nguyen (Redwood AE), Mateo Rios (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Emberstone Head of Product), Tommy Ruiz (Emberstone Staff Eng), Aisha Khan (Emberstone CTO)

Summary (auto):
Quick qualification of Emberstone's use-case (user-facing summarization and content generation in-app), comparison of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, ask for time-to-first-token & free credits for a pilot, security questions (SAML/SOC2/KMS), and next steps to run a short benchmark.

Topics:
- PLG/self-serve path and free credits
- Time-to-first-token and SDK onboarding
- Dedicated capacity for predictability vs Hosted for speed
- Security: SSO, SOC2, data retention, KMS
- Pilot scope and success metrics

Transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sarah from Redwood. Can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Janelle Park: Yep, Janelle here, Head of Product at Emberstone. We build a content summarization feature inside our authoring suite.
[00:13] Tommy Ruiz: Tommy, staff eng, I own infra and integrations.
[00:16] Aisha Khan: Aisha, CTO, listening for security and cost implications.
[00:20] Sarah Nguyen: Great. Mateo from our SE team will cover technical bits. Mateo?
[00:23] Mateo Rios: Hey all, quick hello. Happy to dive into latency, batching, and any perf questions.
[00:28] Sarah Nguyen: Goal today — understand your constraints, recommend a path: self-serve Hosted quickstart with free credits, or move towards Dedicated or Private if needed. Also time-to-first-token expectations.

[00:40] Janelle Park: High level: we need fast summaries for authors, 200–300ms token generation is ideal at p95 for the UI, but we can tolerate up to 600ms if cost is better. Goal is to A/B test model variants this quarter. We'll likely start with a PLG pilot.

[01:05] Tommy Ruiz: To add, our current infra is on GCP, we use GKE and have strict network egress rules. If we go Hosted we'd need a VPC peering or egress allowances. Private deploy is possible but we want to avoid on-prem complexity initially.

[01:28] Mateo Rios: Makes sense. For p95 latencies like that, Hosted on Redwood often meets the fast path—our shared Hosted endpoints are optimized and we auto-route to low-latency regions. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower jitter, but you'd commit.

[01:45] Aisha Khan: What about data residency and encryption? We need SOC 2 and KMS integration at minimum.

[01:52] Sarah Nguyen: We have SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we use tenant-level separation and encryption-at-rest, and we can provide audit logs. If you need customer-managed keys, that's part of Private.

[02:12] Janelle Park: Okay. About free credits — what's typical? We want to run a pilot that hits maybe 30k tokens/day for 2 weeks to get baseline metrics.

[02:22] Sarah Nguyen: We offer starter credits for PLG pilots; for something like 30k tokens/day for two weeks, we can cover that under our onramp credits. We'll confirm in the follow-up email.

[02:36] Tommy Ruiz: On-boarding — how fast can we get an engineer from repo to first token? We're looking for a 1–2 day PSP, ideally.

[02:44] Mateo Rios: Typical self-serve time-to-first-token is under an hour if you use our SDK and quickstart. For teams running network policies it can be a bit longer — we have a small script to test connectivity and a benchmark script we can share.

[03:02] Janelle Park: Can you show us an SDK snippet now?

[03:06] Mateo Rios: Sure, short one: import redwood, client = redwood.Client(api_key=...), resp = client.generate(prompt="summarize this...") — returns streamed tokens. We'll attach language-specific examples, Node, Python, and a curl example in the doc.

[03:28] Aisha Khan: Streaming is important for UX. Also do you support function-calling or structured output?

[03:34] Mateo Rios: Yes, function-calling-like structured outputs are supported; we also have deterministic sampling controls to stabilize summaries. There's also built-in token accounting in console.

[03:50] Tommy Ruiz: On tooling — we need metrics: token-level cost, latency per route, and per-model breakdown.

[03:58] Sarah Nguyen: Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards, token cost heatmaps, and traces. You can set alerts on regressions tied to prompt sets.

[04:12] Janelle Park: Let's talk about Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for us. We want predictable cost and capacity if we scale.

[04:20] Mateo Rios: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools, you get predictable throughput and isolation. If your traffic is spiky but predictable paging, Dedicated helps avoid noisy neighbor variance. Hosted is better if you want low setup friction and you prefer usage-based billing.

[04:38] Aisha Khan: If we pick Dedicated, what's the typical lead time and contract?

[04:44] Sarah Nguyen: Lead time can be a couple of weeks depending on the region and capacity. Contracts are monthly/annual commits. For pilots we usually keep customers on Hosted or a small Dedicated burst config.

[04:58] Tommy Ruiz: Any special network setup for Dedicated? We're trying to avoid opening wide egress.

[05:04] Mateo Rios: Dedicated in cloud region can be in your VPC (Private mode) with secure peering, and we support private link in some clouds. For strict egress we can prep a private deployment package but that adds to setup time.

[05:20] Janelle Park: How do you handle model versioning and rollouts? We need canary tests before full deploy.

[05:26] Mateo Rios: Rollouts are native: you can pin model versions, do canary percentages, A/B, and configure automatic fallback to a baseline variant on errors. Evals tie to prompt sets so you can detect regressions.

[05:44] Sarah Nguyen: Quick question, what success metrics will you use for the pilot? Latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality thresholds right?

[05:50] Janelle Park: Yes — p95 latency <500ms, summary ROUGE-like acceptability of >0.75 on our internal set, and cost target under $X/1k tokens — we'll share the exact number.

[06:08] Tommy Ruiz: We want to run a quick time-to-first-token test. Mateo, can you outline the steps?

[06:13] Mateo Rios: Sure: 1) Create a free account, 2) redeem pilot credits, 3) copy API key, 4) run our small connectivity script (we'll send), 5) call the generate endpoint with your prompt set and measure end-to-end. That should take under an hour if network is open.

[06:32] Aisha Khan: Does the quickstart require opening ports or just outbound HTTPS?

[06:35] Mateo Rios: Only outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai endpoints — no inbound required. If you need VPC peering that's separate.

[06:44] Janelle Park: On cost: do you have guidance on batching and tokenization to reduce unit cost?

[06:49] Mateo Rios: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends batching configuration and prefix caching. For summarization you can cache document embeddings and reuse KV cache to cut costs. We also give quantization recommendations if you deploy Dedicated/Private.

[07:05] Tommy Ruiz: Are there any limits on free credits usage like rate limits or model restrictions?

[07:11] Sarah Nguyen: Starter credits have standard rate limits to prevent abuse, and we can raise them temporarily for bench runs. Some paid model variants might be excluded; we'll specify in the follow-up.

[07:26] Janelle Park: Security details — can you share SOC 2 report and details on audit logs?

[07:31] Sarah Nguyen: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 and architecture security docs. Audit logs are available in Private and Dedicated; Hosted has tenant logs and we can export audit trails on request.

[07:46] Aisha Khan: KMS—if we want customer-managed keys, is that only with Private?

[07:52] Mateo Rios: Correct, CMKs and HSM integrations are part of the Private package. Hosted uses our managed keys with encryption-at-rest.

[08:02] Tommy Ruiz: What about rate limiting and throttles? We have bursty events.

[08:07] Sarah Nguyen: You can define per-route quotas, spikes can be handled with burst capacity on Dedicated, and automated fallback policies can degrade to a cheaper model variant during overload.

[08:21] Janelle Park: Any examples of other media companies using Redwood for real-time summarization?

[08:27] Sarah Nguyen: We have a few anonymized case studies — we'll include a short summary in the follow-up email.

[08:36] Tommy Ruiz: Benchmarks — do you have a simple script for token latency and p95?

[08:40] Mateo Rios: Yes, we'll attach a small Node/Python script that hits the generate endpoint with streaming and records p50/p95/p99. It includes warm-up to ensure KV cache effects are present.

[09:00] Janelle Park: For our pilot we want to test both Hosted and a small Dedicated config. Is that feasible cost-wise?

[09:07] Sarah Nguyen: Absolutely, we often run hybrid pilots — start Hosted for speed-to-first-read and then spin up a small Dedicated pool to compare. We'll show you cost deltas.

[09:20] Aisha Khan: If we do Private later, what's the migration path?

[09:24] Mateo Rios: Migration is straightforward: you pin model versions and route traffic to your Private endpoints. All rolling policies and configs carry over. It just requires provisioning the Private control plane and hooking up your KMS/SSO.

[09:38] Tommy Ruiz: Any gotchas with tokenization differences across models?

[09:42] Mateo Rios: Yes, tokenization varies by model — we provide tokenizers in SDK and the console breaks down tokens by model so you can align prompts. That helps avoid surprises in cost.

[09:56] Janelle Park: How do you handle content moderation / safety? We need to filter certain outputs.

[10:01] Sarah Nguyen: Redwood provides optional content filters and safety hooks. You can run outputs through our reranking or integrate your own post-processing. For enterprise we'd recommend routing through a safe-check pipeline.

[10:14] Aisha Khan: Legal — any model licensing restrictions we should know about?

[10:18] Sarah Nguyen: We'll surface model-level licensing in the model catalog; some open models have specific attribution or commercial use clauses. We'll include a note.

[10:28] Tommy Ruiz: On observability, can we get trace-level spans for token generation?

[10:33] Mateo Rios: Yes, we support tracing hooks and can send traces to your preferred APM. Token-level breakdowns are in the console.

[10:46] Janelle Park: Great. For the pilot's success criteria, we'll share prompts and expected thresholds. Any recommended model to start with for summarization?

[10:55] Mateo Rios: Our catalog recommends a mid-sized instruction-tuned model for balance of latency and quality; we'll suggest two variants: economy (lower cost) and high-quality (slower, better ROUGE).

[11:12] Sarah Nguyen: About rollout — we can run a 2-week Hosted pilot using credits, measure p95 + quality, then do a 1-week Dedicated smoke test. If that looks good we can talk commits.

[11:26] Janelle Park: Sounds good. Anything else we should be aware of?

[11:30] Tommy Ruiz: One more thing — do you support IP allowlisting for API keys?

[11:34] Mateo Rios: Yes, you can set IP allowlists per key, and we support short-lived keys for integration security.

[11:43] Aisha Khan: What's the SLA for Hosted vs Dedicated?

[11:47] Sarah Nguyen: Hosted has standard uptime guarantees; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets at certain commit tiers. We'll include SLA doc.

[11:58] Janelle Park: Okay recap?

[12:00] Sarah Nguyen: Recap: 1) Redwood will provide PLG starter credits for a 2-week Hosted pilot covering ~30k tokens/day; 2) Mateo will send quickstart + benchmark script; 3) Sarah will send tailored pricing and Dedicated config options; 4) Emberstone will share prompt sets and target metrics.

[12:20] Tommy Ruiz: We'll aim to run initial time-to-first-token test tomorrow, barring firewall hops.

[12:25] Sarah Nguyen: Great — I'll follow up with everything and links. Thanks all.

[12:30] Janelle Park: Thanks, excited to try it.

[12:32] Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone.

[12:35] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word swaps (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), some speaker overlaps, timestamps approximate every 30–90s.
